reference.source: Firestein & Kelley's Textbook of Rheumatology / Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine
clinicalPearls: A rare autoimmune vasculitic disorder combining inflammatory eye disease with audiovestibular dysfunction, usually in young adults
The classic ocular feature is interstitial keratitis causing photophobia, eye pain, redness, and blurred vision, though scleritis and uveitis also occur
Inner ear involvement resembles Meniere disease with sudden sensorineural hearing loss, vertigo, and tinnitus, and can progress to deafness
Ocular and audiovestibular features may not appear simultaneously, so a high index of suspicion is needed when one precedes the other
A systemic large-vessel vasculitis, including aortitis and aortic valve involvement, complicates a proportion of cases
There is no specific diagnostic test; diagnosis is clinical after excluding infective causes such as syphilis
Prompt systemic corticosteroids are the mainstay for hearing preservation, with immunosuppressive or biologic agents in refractory or systemic disease
reference.pathophysiology: Cogan syndrome is regarded as an autoimmune vasculitis, possibly triggered by preceding infection, in which the immune response cross-reacts with shared antigens in the cornea and inner ear. Autoantibodies directed against inner ear and endothelial antigens have been described. Immune-mediated inflammation of the corneal stroma produces interstitial keratitis, while inflammation and damage to the cochlea and vestibular apparatus cause hearing loss and vertigo. In some patients the process extends to a systemic vasculitis affecting large vessels, leading to aortitis and aortic regurgitation.
additionalDifferentials: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis and other systemic vasculitides
additionalInvestigations: Slit-lamp examination to identify interstitial keratitis, scleritis, or uveitis
Audiometry and vestibular testing to characterise and monitor audiovestibular involvement
Serological testing to exclude syphilis and other infective causes
Inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) and autoimmune screen
Echocardiography and vascular imaging when aortitis or aortic valve disease is suspected
MRI of the brain and inner ear to exclude alternative pathology
redFlags: Rapidly progressive sensorineural hearing loss threatening permanent deafness
Signs of aortitis or new aortic regurgitation indicating systemic vasculitis
Neurological features suggesting central nervous system involvement or an alternative diagnosis
Systemic vasculitic manifestations requiring urgent immunosuppression
reference.prognosis: With prompt corticosteroid therapy ocular inflammation usually settles, but hearing loss is frequently permanent and may progress to bilateral deafness; associated large-vessel vasculitis and aortic valve disease carry additional morbidity and mortality.
pitfalls: Delaying corticosteroids and losing the window to preserve hearing
Attributing audiovestibular symptoms to Meniere disease and missing the ocular link
Failing to exclude syphilis before diagnosing autoimmune interstitial keratitis
Not screening for systemic and aortic vasculitic complications
Managing eye and ear disease in isolation without recognising the unifying diagnosis
management: First-line systemic corticosteroids for audiovestibular involvement and systemic vasculitis, with topical corticosteroids and cycloplegics for interstitial keratitis
Prompt high-dose corticosteroids for sudden sensorineural hearing loss in an attempt to preserve hearing

Steroid-sparing immunosuppression such as methotrexate, azathioprine, ciclosporin, mycophenolate or cyclophosphamide, and biologics such as TNF inhibitors, tocilizumab or rituximab for refractory or systemic disease
Exclude infective mimics, particularly syphilis, before committing to immunosuppression
Cochlear implantation for progressive bilateral deafness, and cardiothoracic surgery for aortitis or aortic valve disease
Monitor with serial audiometry and vestibular testing, inflammatory markers, and echocardiography or vascular imaging for large-vessel and valvular complications
Multidisciplinary care across rheumatology, ophthalmology, ENT and audiology, and cardiology
Escalate rapidly for acute hearing loss, uncontrolled ocular inflammation or evolving large-vessel vasculitis
